domain: Finding paying customers (businesses) for products that already exist, for example barbers for the appointment system
mission: Own the pipeline of businesses that could pay for an existing product: who has the problem, the public signal, a lawful and honest first message as a draft, and whether prospects become paying regulars. This is not about people who want a project built for them; that is Projects Scout.

data_questions.q: Which product and which buyer type are we finding for, and what verified claim makes the offer true?
Which public buying signals were found, from which allowed sources, with dates?
Of earlier prospects, how many replied, became leads, became regular paying customers (aggregates only) or 'too little data'?
Which channel rules (consent, opt-out, anti-spam) apply to each candidate's channel in Israel?
What do the numbers of this domain say (trend, anomaly, denominator, sample size), what conclusion do they support, and what would change next run because of it?

rules: Public business information only; no personal profiles, no scraping behind logins
Every draft message includes an opt-out and a true reason for contact
Personal data never goes to git; prospects stay in git-ignored files
Lawyer check is a named open item before any cold outreach
Every claim traces to a verified line in the product file; demo data is labelled
Nothing leaves the system without Yotam's per-action approval

produce.instructions: List candidates with evidence and write draft outreach into business/prospects/{date}.md (git-ignored). Nothing is sent.

gates.cmd: ! git check-ignore -q business/prospects/{date}.md && { echo 'prospects file is not git-ignored'; exit 1; } || exit 0

benchmark.task: Find and qualify 5 candidate customers for one product from public information, with draft outreach.

rubric.q: Does each candidate have a dated public signal?
Are opt-out, consent and lawful basis handled in every draft?
Is each candidate truly a buyer of this product?
Is the draft specific, short and honest?
